title: Lisse sheaves of modules are module objects in finite locally constant sheaves of sets
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a finite ring (not necessarily commutative). Call a sheaf $\mathcal F$ of left $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site $Y_{\Et}$ *lisse* if there are an etale covering $\{U_i\to Y\}$ and finite left $\Lambda$-modules $M_i$ with $\mathcal F|_{U_i}\cong\underline{M_i}_{U_i}$ as sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules, where $\underline M$ is the sheafification of the constant presheaf $U\mapsto M$. Write $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ for the category of finite locally constant sheaves of sets on $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]; it has finite products (computed in all sheaves of sets) and the final object $\underline{\{*\}}$. A *$\Lambda$-module object* of $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ is an object $\mathcal A$ with morphisms $+:\mathcal A\times\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$, $0:\underline{\{*\}}\to\mathcal A$, $-:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ and $\lambda\cdot:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$, satisfying the axioms of a left $\Lambda$-module written as commutative diagrams; a morphism of $\Lambda$-module objects is a morphism of $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ commuting with these maps. Then:

1. A sheaf of left $\Lambda$-modules on $Y_{\Et}$ is lisse if and only if its underlying sheaf of sets lies in $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$.
2. The functor sending a lisse sheaf $\mathcal F$ to its underlying sheaf of sets with the addition, zero, negation and scalar multiplications of $\mathcal F$ is an equivalence (indeed an isomorphism) from the category of lisse sheaves of left $\Lambda$-modules, with $\Lambda$-linear maps of sheaves, onto the category of $\Lambda$-module objects of $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$.

proof.text: If $\mathcal F$ is lisse, choose an etale covering on which it is isomorphic, as a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules, to the constant sheaf of a finite left $\Lambda$-module $M_i$. Forgetting the module structure gives an isomorphism of sheaves of sets with the constant finite sheaf underlying $M_i$, so the underlying sheaf lies in $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$.

source.place: Lemma 0DV5, proof of (1) in the locally constant case

proof.text: Conversely, suppose the underlying sheaf of sets of a sheaf of left $\Lambda$-modules $\mathcal F$ is finite locally constant. Trivialize the underlying sheaf on an etale cover, and also trivialize the finite products that occur as operation sources. For any one of the finitely many operations, each element of its finite constant source has an image section of the finite constant target; after an etale refinement that image is a specified constant section, and refining simultaneously over the finite source makes the operation a map of finite constant sets. Since there are only finitely many operations (because $\Lambda$ is finite), one common refinement makes all of them constant maps. The module axioms already hold as sheaf-map equalities, so the induced finite maps satisfy them; the local constant finite set is therefore a finite left $\Lambda$-module and the local identification is an isomorphism of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules, proving that $\mathcal F$ is lisse.

The construction from a lisse sheaf to its underlying sheaf with its given operations is inverse to the construction in the preceding step: forgetting and then restoring the operations leaves every operation unchanged, while a module object of $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ already has exactly the corresponding sheaf-of-modules structure. A morphism is preserved and recovered precisely when it commutes with addition, zero, negation, and scalar multiplication. Hence the two categories and their morphisms are identified, so the functor in (2) is an isomorphism (and therefore an equivalence).
